output.sql:
SELECT order_month, COUNT(*) AS completed_orders
FROM marts.fct_orders
WHERE is_revenue
  AND order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
  AND order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY order_month
ORDER BY completed_orders DESC, order_month
FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS WITH TIES
output.explanation: Counts completed orders (is_revenue) per month of 2024 and returns the month with the highest count. If several months tie for the most, all of them are returned. PostgreSQL's WITH TIES treats rows as tied only when they match on every ORDER BY column, so the month tiebreaker means only the earliest tied month is returned.
